name: canRaise-restates-the-law-instead-of-asking-it
why: The restatement agrees with statUp everywhere except its clamp, which is exactly where a player would be offered a press the law refuses.

name: a-press-does-not-aim-before-it-presses
why: ORL1's incident one layer up: a press that acts on whatever the cursor was left on raises the wrong attribute, silently, on every click.

name: the-HIGHEST-major-is-dropped-from-the-sum
old: for (const id of majors) if (value(id) < value(lowest)) lowest = id;
new: for (const id of majors) if (value(id) > value(lowest)) lowest = id;
why: The ribbon would teach a player the opposite of PlayerEntity.SetCurrentLevelUpSkillSum.

name: the-WORST-minor-is-the-one-that-counts
old: for (const id of minors) if (value(id) > value(best)) best = id;
new: for (const id of minors) if (value(id) < value(best)) best = id;

name: the-oghma-is-promised-a-level-it-does-not-grant
why: applyLevelUp's oghma arm takes no Level++ (AUDIT 39), so this is the window lying about the one thing it is for.

name: the-commit-is-allowed-with-points-unspent
why: DFU's CheckIfDoneLeveling and the mod's validateLevelUp are the same sentence: all of it, or nothing. Re-aimed BY CONTENT when LV1's audit added IsAllMax's second term to the same line.

name: two-stars-are-drawn-on-the-same-point
why: The figure is stretched to the stage, so a pair this close is two overlapping buttons on a phone - a point spent on the wrong attribute.

name: a-fortified-attribute-overflows-its-star
old: export const starBrightness = (value) => Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (value ?? 0) / MAX_STAT_VALUE));

name: the-enhanced-skin-loses-its-level-up-window
old: if (isEnhanced() && typeof document !== 'undefined') return enhancedLevelUpOverlay(rollout(), deps.entity);

name: the-font-less-escape-cannot-recognise-the-DOM-window
why: scenes/dungeonContext.js asks by this name; a window it cannot recognise is nulled rather than closed, and stays on the screen over a game already handed back.

name: the-window-forgets-CheckIfDoneLevelings-second-term
why: The wall LV1's audit found: at 100 across the board every press is refused, the pool never reaches zero, and an exit that tests zero alone never opens.

name: the-canvas-screen-keeps-the-wall
why: ui/charsheet.js's LevelUpScreen is what the enhanced skin mounted until LV1 and what it still mounts headless; the sheet's own rollout has had the term since AUDIT 44.

name: a-maxed-character-is-told-to-take-a-point-back
why: An instruction with no elsewhere in it - there is nothing to take back and nowhere to put it.

name: the-sheet-keeps-a-second-copy-of-IsAllMax
why: ONE DFU MEMBER, ONE EXPORT: the copy is what let LevelUpScreen ship without the law at all.

name: willpower-cites-the-display-instead-of-the-consumer
why: A display is not evidence that a number does anything; the blurb is a promise about code that runs.

name: the-repaint-rebuilds-the-whole-sheet-on-every-keystroke
why: riseRibbon and sheetModel - gold, encumbrance, thirty-five skills, the class specials - on the keyboard's repeat rate, for two fields the repaint does not read.

name: the-paused-game-is-blank-again
old: let waitTimer = setTimeout(() => { wait = paintLevelUpWait(host, { oghma: !!screen?.oghma }); }, LEVELUP_WAIT_MS);
why: The window opens because the GAME decided, so a chunk in flight is a frozen frame with nothing on it and nothing the player pressed to explain it.

name: the-wait-outlives-the-window-it-was-waiting-for
old: stopWaiting();   // the window is the wait's successor, and takes the slot before it is torn down

name: the-notice-is-drawn-over-a-wait-that-says-you-have-risen
old: notice: (h, o) => { stopWaiting(); return paintChunkNotice(h, o); },
why: Two answers to one event: 'You have risen.' behind 'This screen could not be loaded.'

name: the-book-is-announced-as-a-level-it-does-not-grant
why: AUDIT 39: the Infinium takes no Level++ and no health roll.

name: the-warm-shouts-about-a-stale-chunk-at-boot
why: An unhandled rejection at boot about a screen nobody has asked for is the silence-and-noise pair ui/enhancedChunk.js exists to get right.

name: a-host-stops-warming-the-level-up-window
old: warmLevelUpWindow();   // LV1's audit: the level-up window opens because the GAME decided, so its chunk warms at boot rather than inside a pause nobody asked for

name: the-chronicle-forgets-the-key-it-is-named-after
why: L opened the window and L did nothing - a press the host consumed and nobody answered (MAC-C's law, the door it was never applied to).

name: the-chronicle-reads-the-literal-instead-of-the-registry
why: A rebound key that cannot close the window it opened is FIX-F's bug one layer down.
